findings.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — [P1/100] `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no maximum, so one mutation can create unbounded attendee rows, locale lookups, calendar updates, and `Promise.all` email work.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — [P1/100] `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` binds calendar mutation to the authorized actor even though the handler admits attendees, so an attendee-initiated guest addition updates with the attendee's credentials rather than the booking organizer's calendar credentials.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:124 — [P2/100] The reconstructed `CalendarEvent` omits `team`, so `sendAddGuestsEmails` can never populate its `calendarEvent.team?.members` notification branch and team hosts are not notified of added guests.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — [P2/100] Passing raw `guests` instead of persisted `uniqueGuests` makes an already-attending address supplied again match the "new guest" branch and receive a fresh scheduling email although no attendee was added.

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:525 — [P1/100] `sendAddGuestsEmails(calEvent, newGuests)` never accepts or checks `disableStandardEmails.all.host`/`disableStandardEmails.all.attendee`, so guest-add notifications are sent even when either corresponding standard-email preference is disabled.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — [P1/100] `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` permits duplicate addresses and the handler passes every accepted entry to `createMany`, so a direct request with the same new address twice persists duplicate attendees.

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:541 — [P2/100] `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` receives raw `guests` rather than the handler's filtered `uniqueGuests`, so submitting an existing attendee alongside one new guest sends that existing attendee an `AttendeeScheduledEmail` as if newly invited instead of the guests-added notice.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — P1/C100 `await prisma.booking.update(...createMany...)` commits new attendee rows before `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` at line 165, so a transient calendar-update failure leaves the booking database ahead of the provider and every retry is rejected by `uniqueGuests`/`if (uniqueGuests.length === 0)`, permanently orphaning those guests from the calendar event.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:47 — P1/C75: `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` requires a team administrator also to be the owner, so an administrator who is not the booking organizer or attendee is rejected with `FORBIDDEN` at line 54.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — P1/C100: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` loads the acting attendee's credentials even though line 52 explicitly authorizes attendees, so their guest-add request attempts to update the organizer's booking with the attendee's calendar integrations.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — P1/C100: `await prisma.booking.update(...)` commits the new attendees before `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(...)` at line 165, so a calendar-provider failure leaves the booking changed locally while the calendar remains unchanged and the mutation errors.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — P2/C100: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` accepts duplicate valid email addresses while line 74 only filters existing attendees, so a direct mutation with `["guest@example.com", "guest@example.com"]` passes the same attendee twice to `createMany` at handler line 102.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:76 — P2/C100: `guest === attendee.email` and `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` compare unnormalized addresses even though the blacklist is lowercased at line 71, so case-variant emails bypass existing-attendee and blacklist exclusion.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — P1/100 `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no cardinality limit, so one request can synchronously create arbitrarily many attendees and trigger unbounded translation, calendar, and email work until the request or providers are exhausted.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — P2/75 `const uniqueGuests = guests.filter(...)` neither de-duplicates input nor serializes against another request's stale attendee snapshot, so duplicate/concurrent additions can create duplicate attendees or surface an unnormalized database uniqueness error.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — P1/100 `await prisma.booking.update(...)` commits the new attendees before the subsequently awaited calendar sync, so a calendar-provider failure returns an error after local state changed and retry is rejected as already-added with no reconciliation path.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — P1/100 `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is caught and discarded by the following `catch`, so rejected/partially completed notification fanout still returns `Guests added` with no retry or user-visible failure.

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:539 — P1/100 `...calendarEvent.attendees.map(...)` eagerly starts one remote send per attendee and `Promise.all` awaits them without concurrency, rate, or timeout control, so a large booking can hang the mutation or overwhelm the mail provider.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is accurate. Looking at the diff, `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` in addGuests.schema.ts defines `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max()` constraint. In addGuests.handler.ts, this unbounded array is used to: 1) create attendee rows via `createMany`, 2) run `Promise.all(attendeesListPromises)` for locale lookups, 3) call `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees()`, and 4) call `sendAddGuestsEmails()` which spawns multiple email promises. adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a real issue in the diff. Looking at addGuests.handler.ts, the code at line 92 does `await prisma.booking.update(...)` with `createMany` to add attendees to the database. Then at line 165, `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` is called. If the calendar update fails, the database already has the new attendees committed. On retry, the `uniqueGuests` filter at lines 68-72 will filter out these guests since they're already in `booking.attendees`, resulting in `uniqueGuests.length === 0` and throwing an error at line 74. This creates a permanent inconsistency where guests exist in the database but not in the calendar, and retries cannot fix it. This is a legitimate transactional consistency bug.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a bug. Looking at the diff, line 52 shows `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` which allows attendees to add guests. However, at line 158, `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` fetches the credentials of the current user (who could be an attendee), and these credentials are then used to create an EventManager and call `updateCalendarAttendees`. This means when an attendee adds guests, the code attempts to update calendar events using the attendee's credentials rather than the organizer's credentials, which would fail or cause incorrect behavior since the attendee doesn't own the calendar event.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — P1/C100: `await prisma.booking.update(...)` commits the new attendees before `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(...)` at line 165, so a calendar-provider failure leaves the booking changed locally while the calendar remains unchanged and the mutation errors.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a transactional consistency issue in addGuests.handler.ts. Looking at the diff, line 92-107 shows `await prisma.booking.update(...)` which commits new attendees to the database. Then at line 165, `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` is called to sync with the calendar provider. If the calendar update fails, the database already has the new attendees but the external calendar doesn't, leaving the system in an inconsistent state. This is a real bug - the operations should either be wrapped in a transaction with rollback capability, or the calendar update should happen first, or there should be compensation logic on failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — P2/C100: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` accepts duplicate valid email addresses while line 74 only filters existing attendees, so a direct mutation with `["guest@example.com", "guest@example.com"]` passes the same attendee twice to `createMany` at handler line 102.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is accurate. Looking at the diff: 1) addGuests.schema.ts line 5 shows `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` which validates emails but doesn't enforce uniqueness. 2) In addGuests.handler.ts, line 74 (the uniqueGuests filter) only filters out emails that already exist in booking.attendees, not duplicates within the input array itself. 3) Line 102 shows `createMany: { data: guestsFullDetails }` which would create duplicate attendee records if the same email appears twice in the input. While the frontend AddGuestsDialog.tsx has a ZAddGuestsInputSchema with uniqueness validation (lines 25-28), this is client-side only. A direct API call could bypass this and submit duplicate emails, which would pass server-side validation and create duplicate attendees.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — P1/100 `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no cardinality limit, so one request can synchronously create arbitrarily many attendees and trigger unbounded translation, calendar, and email work until the request or providers are exhausted.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows ZAddGuestsInputSchema at line 5 defines `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max()` limit. The handler in addGuests.handler.ts processes all guests by creating attendees in the database, calling getTranslation for each attendee, updating calendar via eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees, and sending emails via sendAddGuestsEmails. Without a cardinality limit, a malicious request could pass thousands of email addresses, causing unbounded database writes, translation lookups, calendar API calls, and email sends. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — P2/75 `const uniqueGuests = guests.filter(...)` neither de-duplicates input nor serializes against another request's stale attendee snapshot, so duplicate/concurrent additions can create duplicate attendees or surface an unnormalized database uniqueness error.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the code at line 74 filters guests against existing attendees but doesn't deduplicate the input array itself. If the same email appears twice in the `guests` input array, both would pass the filter and be added via `createMany`. Additionally, there's no database-level uniqueness constraint handling or transaction isolation shown, so concurrent requests could read the same attendee snapshot and both add the same guest. The schema at addGuests.schema.ts only validates that each element is an email, not that they're unique within the array. This is a real correctness bug that could create duplicate attendees.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — P1/100 `await prisma.booking.update(...)` commits the new attendees before the subsequently awaited calendar sync, so a calendar-provider failure returns an error after local state changed and retry is rejected as already-added with no reconciliation path.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a real issue in addGuests.handler.ts. Looking at lines 92-108, the code first does `await prisma.booking.update(...)` to add attendees to the database, then later calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` to sync with the calendar. If the calendar sync fails, the database already has the new attendees committed, but the user gets an error. On retry, the guests would be filtered out by the `uniqueGuests` check (lines 72-76) since they're already in `booking.attendees`, resulting in 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' error with no way to complete the calendar sync. This is a legitimate transactional consistency bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — P1/75 `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` uses the caller's tokens even though an attendee is authorized to invoke this mutation, so an attendee caller can commit the guest list but cannot authenticate the organizer calendar update.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a real issue. Looking at the diff, the addGuests handler at line 47-49 allows attendees to call this mutation (isAttendee check). However, at line 158, `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` fetches the credentials of the caller (ctx.user), not the organizer. When an attendee calls this mutation, their credentials are used for the EventManager.updateCalendarAttendees call at line 165, but attendees don't have credentials to update the organizer's calendar. The organizer's credentials should be used instead (booking.user.credentials is already fetched in the include at line 38). This is a real authorization/functionality bug where attendees can add guests but the calendar update will fail due to using wrong credentials.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — P1/100 `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is caught and discarded by the following `catch`, so rejected/partially completed notification fanout still returns `Guests added` with no retry or user-visible failure.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that in addGuests.handler.ts lines 165-169, the sendAddGuestsEmails call is wrapped in a try-catch that only logs 'Error sending AddGuestsEmails' and then returns success ('Guests added'). This means if email sending fails (partially or completely), the user sees success with no indication of the email failure. While this is a real concern visible in the diff, it's a design decision rather than a bug - the guests ARE added to the database successfully before the email step. However, it's an important architectural concern that silent email failures could leave users unaware that notifications weren't sent. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:58 — P2/100 `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })` turns an existing booking whose nullable/deleted owner has no user row into a raw Prisma 500 instead of a defined tRPC error.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows at line 58 in addGuests.handler.ts: `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — P2/100 `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` imposes no item limit, allowing any authenticated attendee of a booking to submit an arbitrarily large recipient list that is persisted and mailed by `sendAddGuestsEmails`, turning the service into an invitation-spam and resource-exhaustion primitive.
